scene.note: The JSON triage reply is scored one property at a time, so a case earns partial credit and every miss comes with a reason.

value.label: a reply for a wilted orchid

steps.note: The JSON triage model answers with one object: a category, an urgency from 1 to 5, the order id and a one line summary.
contains and matches read the reply as plain text. contains looks for a piece of text exactly as written, case included, and matches tests a pattern with its flags.
fieldEquals and near read one top-level field of the object. fieldEquals wants that exact value, and near wants a number within a tolerance of a target, edges included.

entries.value: '' on a pass, a short sentence on a fail

steps.note: Every grader answers pass and a reason. A failing reason says what was looked for and, for a field, what was found.
A reply with words around the JSON fails the JSON graders with a reason that mentions JSON. The run goes on.
gradeOutput gets one reply and the list of graders for its case.
Every grader runs on the reply, so a case shows all of its problems at once.
A grader that throws counts as a failure whose reason starts with grader error, and the other graders still run.
An empty list of graders is an Error, because a case that checks nothing would always pass.

entries.value: share of graders that passed, 0 to 1
true only when every grader passed

steps.note: Dev gets a number that moves a little when a change helps a little, and a strict flag beside it.

args.input: The courier left my planter at the wrong entrance.

steps.note: Each case lists its checks as plain data: a kind and the settings for that kind.
buildGrader turns a spec into the grader of its kind: contains uses text, regex uses pattern and flags, field uses field and equals, near uses field, value and tolerance.
A kind it does not know, say a typo in the case file, throws an Error that names the kind.
Each input goes through triageJson with the model you were given. Some replies come back wrapped in a code fence.
Each reply is graded with its own case's checks, and the result is kept under the case id, in case order.

entries.value: { id, score, passed, reasons } per case

steps.note: Dev reads one mean score, how many cases fully passed and every failing reason.
